stem: A network performance study measures the download speed (Mbps) for a sample of 30 subscribers. The sample mean is 261.9 Mbps with a sample standard deviation of 78.3 Mbps. However, 2 of the 30 observations appear to be outliers (values more than 2.5 standard deviations from the mean). If these outliers are removed, the remaining 28 observations have a mean of 246.7 Mbps and standard deviation of 58.2 Mbps. Estimate the true population mean and provide a 95% confidence interval that accounts for the uncertainty about whether outliers should be included.

ground_truth.answer: With all data: mean = 261.9, 95% CI = [232.7, 291.1]. Without outliers: mean = 246.7, 95% CI = [224.7, 268.7]. Combined interval accounting for analytic uncertainty: [224.7, 291.1]. Point estimate: 254.3 Mbps.

solution_steps: The outlier treatment choice creates structural uncertainty. Combined interval: [224.7, 291.1].
common_failure_modes: Using only the full sample without considering outlier impact
Removing outliers without reporting both analyses
Not recognizing that the choice of analysis method is itself a source of uncertainty
